Google Cloud's listed product is Google Vertex AI, categorized under cloud ai services & model apis, with unified ML platform as the function this data names first.

The data also tags Google Vertex AI with model Garden, AutoML, MLOps lifecycle, and BigQuery integration, description of what the product does rather than how well it does it. It also notes TPU support, one of the few entries in this set where the product touches compute or physical infrastructure directly rather than sitting purely at the application layer.

Beyond the category, the product name, and this short list of tags tied to cloud.google.com, the data carries no user counts, revenue, funding, or headcount, so nothing here supports a claim about Google Cloud's scale or trajectory.

profile_text.body:
Google Cloud is the cloud computing division of Alphabet Inc., a public company traded under the ticker GOOGL (CIK 0001652044). Its website describes the division as offering AI and cloud computing services that address business challenges across security, data management, and hybrid and multi-cloud environments. The site positions Google Cloud as a provider of a fully managed AI platform with access to over 200 foundation models and an ecosystem of AI partners.

Google Cloud's primary tracked AI product is Google Vertex AI, a unified machine learning platform that incorporates Model Garden, AutoML, MLOps lifecycle tooling, BigQuery integration, and TPU support. The site also describes an Agent Platform, presented as a fully managed AI development environment for building and managing AI applications and agents, with access to Agent Studio and the same pool of 200-plus foundation models. Google Cloud also promotes a suite of Gemini products for businesses and developers, including a Gemini Enterprise application. The site cites Best Buy as a customer example, noting that Best Buy uses Google Cloud generative AI to power virtual assistants that handle customer care tasks such as troubleshooting product issues, changing order delivery and schedules, and managing subscriptions.

The held facts record no litigation or MCP server registry presence for Google Cloud at this time.
